nodes.label: query_20260808_162858_below_is_the_group_comment__deeply_review_and_act.md
nodes.community_name: Q: below is the group comment. Deeply review and act accordingly only if the comments are valid: Starting from the current `main` state and accepted `DEC-0018`, conduct a bounded **pre-split feasibility and leakage stress-test** for the future C1/C2/C3 benchmark design. Required work: * preserve the frozen 17,000 sequence-endpoint universe and existing 40/30/20% MMseqs2 components; * quantify positive-edge distribution across components, endpoint/component degree, hub concentration, and source composition; * determine whether component-disjoint train/dev/test assignments can retain sufficient positive evidence for meaningful C1/C2/C3 evaluation; * evaluate feasibility at 40%, 30%, and 20% identity without yet freezing a split; * stress-test residual cross-component homology, especially substantial local/domain-level similarity that may escape the current ≥80% bidirectional full-length coverage rule; * perform an independent completeness/sensitivity check of the primary 30% MMseqs2 similarity graph to identify potentially missed qualifying edges; * quantify how stricter leakage controls change component structure and retained positive evidence; * explicitly assess whether any proposed C3 regime genuinely supports unseen-protein/family claims. Remain fail-closed. Do not: * create or sample negatives/pseudo-negatives; * materialize the full candidate-pair universe; * construct or freeze train/dev/test splits; * authorize C1/C2/C3 labels; * integrate external diagnostic panels; * perform structural-label work; * train, tune, calibrate, or evaluate models; * change the primary PU-R design. Return a clear governance disposition: whether final split construction is scientifically feasible, under which leakage definition(s), and what claim boundaries must apply. Independently validate all consequential counts, update the report/decision/gate/status artifacts, run targeted tests, then commit and push.

nodes.label: Issue 0003: HuRI Attempted Pair Universe
nodes.rationale: The public HuRI release lacks a complete auditable attempted/evaluable pair universe, so unreported pairs remain unlabeled and the primary design is narrowed to positive-unlabeled inference.

nodes.label: Issue 0004: Provider Count Versus Payload Representation
nodes.rationale: Provider headline counts and downloadable representations measure distinct units; all representations must be retained without forcing agreement.

nodes.label: Issue 0005: SIFTS UniProt Release Alignment
nodes.rationale: The frozen SIFTS and UniProt releases differ, preventing exact structural mapping and structure-derived labels until release alignment is validated.

nodes.label: License Compliance
nodes.rationale: Acquisition and redistribution are explicitly bounded by source-specific license evidence.

nodes.label: Conditional Non-detection
nodes.rationale: Non-detection depends on assay, constructs, orientation, organism, technical evaluability, conditions, and selected population.

nodes.label: Evidence-generation-aware PPI Prioritization
nodes.rationale: The matrix frames the intended contribution as evidence-generation-aware direct-PPI inference and evaluation.

nodes.label: Leakage-controlled Benchmark
nodes.rationale: The proposed benchmark combines clustering, temporal freeze, and assay/source/species/interface/PLM-exposure audits.

nodes.label: Sparse Routing
nodes.rationale: The matrix makes sparse routing a conditional architectural contribution contingent on prespecified gates.

nodes.label: TLS Provenance
nodes.rationale: The certificate exception is pinned, hash-recorded, hostname-verifying, and restricted to the Negatome host.

nodes.label: Risk Governance
nodes.rationale: The register records model, infrastructure, data, licensing, and claim risks with mitigations and ownership.

nodes.label: Immutable Release
nodes.rationale: Release candidates and final releases are immutable, versioned packages with governance prerequisites.

nodes.label: Versioned Data Contracts
nodes.rationale: Generated tables must carry schema name, version, and SHA-256 metadata.

nodes.label: Canonical Auditable Mapping
nodes.rationale: Canonical tables are deterministic and auditable while preserving source-native identifiers and conflicts.

nodes.label: Source-native Staging
nodes.rationale: Staging retains audit-useful provider material without classifying it as canonical interaction evidence.

nodes.label: Evidence-record-first Warehouse
nodes.rationale: The warehouse treats source evidence records, rather than provider pair lists, as its primary object.

nodes.label: Universal Nonbinding Prohibition
nodes.rationale: The survey concludes that no source establishes universal nonbinding.
